title: What We Still Have to Solve

sourceEvidence.locator: technical core is entangled with questions about who pays
sourceEvidence.excerpt: technical core is entangled with questions about who pays, who decides, which risks are acceptable and how errors are corrected. The history of successful public systems is therefore less a history of perfect foresight than a history of building mechanisms that can notice failure. Aviation became safer through reporting, investigation, standardization and redesign after incidents. Modern monetary systems use central banks, deposit insurance and supervision because banking panics cannot be preven
